issues.description: Wire message string 'Close' contradicts PR description and Deepgram docs which specify 'CloseStream'.
issues.detail: _CLOSE_MSG sends {"type": "Close"} but the PR text and Deepgram Speak/Listen V1 docs cite {"type": "CloseStream"}. Either the patch does not do what it claims or the description lies. Reconcile against the actual API before merge — this is the load-bearing fact of the entire fix.

issues.description: Single ws.receive() with 1s timeout is not a drain — it returns on the first arbitrary frame.
issues.detail: The stated goal is to flush pending audio before close, but one receive() resolves on any frame (audio chunk, ping, ack). Either loop until a Close/CloseResponse frame bounded by an overall timeout budget, or document this explicitly as a best-effort grace period, not a handshake.

issues.description: Bare 'except Exception' around send/receive conflates expected disconnects with real bugs.
issues.detail: Catching Exception and logging a warning makes ConnectionResetError, protocol errors, and programming bugs indistinguishable. Narrow to ConnectionError / aiohttp.ClientError / asyncio.TimeoutError and mirror the STT plugin's existing handling rather than inventing a new pattern.

issues.description: Protocol constants duplicated on the class instead of shared with the STT plugin.
issues.detail: _FLUSH_MSG and _CLOSE_MSG are protocol-level control frames that STT presumably already defines. Two parallel copies of the same wire vocabulary invite drift. Lift to a shared module-level dict of control messages reused by both plugins, and add a literate comment citing the Deepgram Speak V1 spec.

issues.description: 1.0s timeout is an unmeasured magic number with no rationale.
issues.detail: The PR claims this prevents lingering 429s, but 1.0s is unjustified — possibly too short under jitter (defeating the fix) or too long on hot paths (latency tax). Promote to a named constant with rationale, cite the measurement that produced it, or expose it as configurable.

issues.description: _close_ws complects flush, close handshake, and socket teardown into one method.
issues.detail: Flush (drain audio) and Close (end session) are distinct semantic operations with different time meanings. Decompose into _flush, _drain_until_closed, and _close so the time model is explicit rather than implicit in a single 1s receive plus broad except.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges: the fix is directionally correct (explicit close handshake mirroring STT) but ships with a load-bearing contradiction — the code sends {"type":"Close"} while the PR description and Deepgram docs specify "CloseStream". The single ws.receive() with a 1s timeout is a guess, not a drain, and the bare except Exception erases the difference between expected disconnects and real bugs. Protocol constants should be shared with the STT plugin rather than duplicated, and the close method complects flush, drain, and teardown. Reconcile the wire string, narrow the exception, drain properly, and dedupe constants before merge.
